VERIDANE - INTERNAL - Product Safety Committee memo PSC-2026-07
Date: 2 Oct 2026     From: Elena Kowalczyk, VP Quality & Product Safety     To: Executive Leadership Team

Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.
- Issue: diaphragm seat can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions, allowing gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. 17 field reports of gas odor; 2 reports of delayed ignition causing cabinet damage; no injuries reported.
- Root cause: change of diaphragm compound supplier (Q1 2025); supplier lot material out of spec on compression set. Corrective action complete; replacement valves shipping from Mequon plant since 28 Sep.
- Regulatory: CPSC Fast Track filed 22 Sep; joint recall notice expected the week of 19 Oct. Canada (Health Canada) notification filed.
- Cost: reserve booked in Q3 $21.6M (field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement, logistics). Range $18-26M. Supplier recovery claim of ~$9M lodged, not recognised.
- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

The shift in our business toward data-center thermal infrastructure accelerated again in the third quarter, and it is now unambiguously the growth engine of Veridane. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) net sales grew 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards during the quarter, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% from a year ago. Total company backlog rose 13.0% to $918.0 million, the highest in our history, giving us visibility well into fiscal 2027.

At the same time, this was one of the most challenging quarters we have navigated. Core commercial HVAC demand remained soft, the voluntary GV-400 recall weighed on results, and we reported adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, and adjusted EPS of $0.15. On a GAAP basis, which reflects the recall and restructuring charges, we recorded a net loss of $15.6 million, or $(0.37) per diluted share; the summary financial table accompanying this letter reconciles the two. We are attacking our cost base with urgency through Project Keystone, which targets $35 million of run-rate savings by the end of the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, with two new hyperscale awards won in the quarter.
- Data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 recall executed quickly and transparently: corrective action complete and replacement valves shipping from our Mequon plant since 28 September, with no injuries reported.
- Project Keystone launched, with $6.2 million of restructuring charges taken in the quarter against a $35 million run-rate savings target by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Building Controls & Valves (BCV).** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year. The decline reflects continued softness in commercial construction and retrofit activity, together with a temporary pause in new GV-400 orders from three OEM customers pending the recall notice. Our BCV backlog of $343.8 million was essentially flat year over year, up 0.6%.

During the quarter we initiated a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves sold to OEMs for use in commercial rooftop units and unit heaters. This was a proactive, customer-first action taken in cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program, with a parallel notification filed with Health Canada. The root cause — a supplier lot of diaphragm compound that was out of specification on compression set, introduced with a compound change made in the first quarter of calendar 2025 — has been identified and corrected. No injuries have been reported. Replacement valves are shipping from Mequon, and we recorded a reserve of $21.6 million in the third quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement and logistics. Our three OEM customers are being supported directly, and we are working to restore normal order patterns as the recall notice is published.

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC).** Net sales grew 13.4% to $156.3 million, driven by hyperscale and colocation demand for both air- and liquid-cooled infrastructure. We won two new hyperscale awards in the quarter, and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger introduced in the second quarter is now in service with two hyperscale customers. TDC backlog grew 22.0% year over year to $574.2 million, the strongest indicator we have of fiscal 2027 revenue, and we are prioritizing capacity and tooling for this business within our capital envelope.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to reflect the softer BCV environment, the recall-related order pause and the pace of Keystone realization. We now expect net sales of $1.66-1.70 billion, compared with our prior range of $1.78-1.84 billion, and adjusted EBITDA of $205-215 million, compared with our prior range of $255-270 million.

Project Keystone is our primary earnings lever. The program, which generated $6.2 million of restructuring charges this quarter, encompasses facility consolidation, sourcing and supply-chain redesign, and overhead reduction. Savings begin to build in the fourth quarter and reach the full $35 million run rate by the end of the second quarter of fiscal 2027. Together with completion of the recall program and the increasing weight of TDC in our mix, these actions underpin margin recovery into fiscal 2027.

As of September 30, 2026, we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q.

## Closing

This quarter demanded a great deal from our people — quality, plant, field service and customer-facing teams moved within days to stand behind a product issue and to protect our customers. That is the standard we hold ourselves to, and it is the same discipline we are applying to our cost structure and to the growth engine in data-center cooling. We thank our employees around the world, our customers and our suppliers for their partnership, and our shareholders for their patience and support.

Dana Whitcombe
President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander
EVP & Chief Financial Officer

4 November 2026

# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. — Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders

**Quarter ended 30 September 2026 | FIRST DRAFT — NOT FOR RELEASE. Prepared by IR drafting (ticket IR-2026-Q3-014) for review by Dana, Mark and Priya.**

---

> ### DRAFTING NOTE — DECISION REQUIRED BEFORE RELEASE (remove this block before release)
>
> **Liquidity disclosure — Mark's 14 Oct guidance conflicts with the 12 Oct IR brief and with the legal-approved language.**
>
> Mark's 14 Oct email replaces item 3 of Priya's brief and asks us to (a) leave the credit agreement, waiver request and Note 2 out of the letter, (b) drop the GC-approved liquidity paragraph, and (c) let quarter-end cash stand as the whole liquidity discussion. **This draft does not do that.** It keeps the paragraph approved by K. Brandt (12 Oct) verbatim in the Outlook section.
>
> Why I could not draft it as instructed: at 30 September 2026 we were out of compliance with both financial maintenance covenants (per the draft compliance certificate), the waiver/amendment had not been obtained, and Hartwell Pryce's draft Note 2 states that these conditions raise substantial doubt about going concern. Presenting "$96.4 million of cash" as the company's liquidity position, with no mention of the covenant default or waiver request, would be materially misleading by omission (Rule 10b-5) — particularly with four analyst questions already in the Q&A prep on covenants, lender support and going concern (Q04, Q10, Q14, Q16). If the amendment is executed before the release, the language can be revisited **with the General Counsel**, but as of today the 10-Q draft note stands.
>
> **Other items needing a decision:** see the notes block at the end of this file.
>
> ---

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

The shift in our business toward data-center thermal infrastructure accelerated again in the third quarter, and it is now unambiguously the growth engine of Veridane. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) net sales grew 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards during the quarter, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% from a year ago. Total company backlog rose 13.0% to $918.0 million, the highest in our history, giving us visibility well into fiscal 2027.

At the same time, this was one of the most challenging quarters we have navigated. Core commercial HVAC demand remained soft, the voluntary GV-400 recall weighed on results, and we reported adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, and adjusted EPS of $0.15. On a GAAP basis, which reflects the recall and restructuring charges, we recorded a net loss of $15.6 million, or $(0.37) per diluted share; the summary financial table accompanying this letter reconciles the two. Free cash flow was negative $11.3 million for the quarter, reflecting lower earnings, the recall and working capital; we expect those pressures to ease as recall cash costs roll off and Keystone actions take hold. We are attacking our cost base with urgency through Project Keystone, which targets $35 million of run-rate savings by the end of the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, with two new hyperscale awards won in the quarter.
- Data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 recall executed quickly and transparently: corrective action complete and replacement valves shipping from our Mequon plant since 28 September, with no injuries reported.
- Project Keystone launched, with $6.2 million of restructuring charges taken in the quarter against a $35 million run-rate savings target by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Building Controls & Valves (BCV).** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year. The decline reflects continued softness in commercial construction and retrofit activity, together with a temporary pause in new GV-400 orders from three OEM customers pending the recall notice. Our BCV backlog of $343.8 million was essentially flat year over year, up 0.6%.

During the quarter we initiated a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves sold to OEMs for use in commercial rooftop units and unit heaters. This was a proactive, customer-first action taken in cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program, with a parallel notification filed with Health Canada. The root cause — a supplier lot of diaphragm compound that was out of specification on compression set, introduced with a compound change made in the first quarter of calendar 2025 — has been identified and corrected. No injuries have been reported. Replacement valves are shipping from Mequon, and we recorded a reserve of $21.6 million in the third quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement and logistics. Our three OEM customers are being supported directly, and we are working to restore normal order patterns as the recall notice is published.

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC).** Net sales grew 13.4% to $156.3 million, driven by hyperscale and colocation demand for both air- and liquid-cooled infrastructure. We won two new hyperscale awards in the quarter, and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger introduced in the second quarter is now in service with two hyperscale customers. TDC backlog grew 22.0% year over year to $574.2 million, the strongest indicator we have of fiscal 2027 revenue, This backlog converts to revenue over the next several quarters, with shipments building through the remainder of fiscal 2026 and into fiscal 2027, and we are prioritizing capacity and tooling for this business within our existing capital envelope.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to reflect the softer BCV environment, the recall-related order pause and the pace of Keystone realization. We now expect net sales of $1.66-1.70 billion, compared with our prior range of $1.78-1.84 billion, and adjusted EBITDA of $205-215 million, compared with our prior range of $255-270 million.

Project Keystone is our primary earnings lever. The program, which generated $6.2 million of restructuring charges this quarter, encompasses facility consolidation, sourcing and supply-chain redesign, and overhead reduction. Savings begin to build in the fourth quarter and reach the full $35 million run rate by the end of the second quarter of fiscal 2027. Together with completion of the recall program and the increasing weight of TDC in our mix, these actions underpin margin recovery into fiscal 2027.

As of September 30, 2026, we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q.

## Closing

This quarter demanded a great deal from our people — quality, plant, field service and customer-facing teams moved within days to stand behind a product issue and to protect our customers. That is the standard we hold ourselves to, and it is the same discipline we are applying to our cost structure and to the growth engine in data-center cooling. We are managing this company for the durable franchise it is becoming: a data-center cooling business growing at double digits on top of a core that we are fixing with speed and candour.

We thank our employees around the world, our customers and our suppliers for their partnership, and our shareholders for their patience and support.

Dana Whitcombe
President & Chief Executive Officer

Mark Ostrander
EVP & Chief Financial Officer

4 November 2026

---

*Forward-looking statements: This letter contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, including statements regarding our backlog, guidance, cost-savings programs, the recall, liquidity and our covenant discussions. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied. See "Risk Factors" in our Annual Report on Form 10-K filed with the SEC.*

---

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

The shift in our business toward data-center thermal infrastructure accelerated again in the third quarter, and it is now unambiguously the growth engine of Veridane. Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC) net sales grew 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards during the quarter, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% from a year ago. Total company backlog rose 13.0% to $918.0 million, giving us visibility well into fiscal 2027.

At the same time, this was one of the most challenging quarters we have navigated. Core commercial HVAC demand remained soft, the voluntary GV-400 recall weighed on results, and we reported adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, and adjusted EPS of $0.15. On a GAAP basis, which reflects the recall and restructuring charges, we recorded a net loss of $15.6 million, or $(0.37) per diluted share; the summary financial table accompanying this letter reconciles the two. Free cash flow was negative $11.3 million for the quarter, reflecting lower earnings, the recall and working capital; we expect those pressures to ease as recall cash costs roll off and Keystone actions take hold. We are attacking our cost base with urgency through Project Keystone, which targets $35 million of run-rate savings by the end of the second quarter of fiscal 2027.

## Highlights

- TDC net sales up 13.4% year over year to $156.3 million, with two new hyperscale awards won in the quarter.
- Data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog of $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- GV-400 recall executed quickly and transparently: corrective action complete and replacement valves shipping from our Mequon plant since 28 September, with no injuries reported.
- Project Keystone launched, with $6.2 million of restructuring charges taken in the quarter against a $35 million run-rate savings target by the end of Q2 FY2027.

## Segment review

**Building Controls & Valves (BCV).** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% year over year. The decline reflects continued softness in commercial construction and retrofit activity, together with a temporary pause in new GV-400 orders from three OEM customers pending the recall notice. Our BCV backlog of $343.8 million was essentially flat year over year, up 0.6%.

During the quarter we initiated a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves sold to OEMs for use in commercial rooftop units and unit heaters. This was a proactive, customer-first action taken in cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program, with a parallel notification filed with Health Canada. The root cause — a supplier lot of diaphragm compound that was out of specification on compression set, introduced with a compound change made in the first quarter of calendar 2025 — has been identified and corrected. No injuries have been reported. Replacement valves are shipping from Mequon, and we recorded a reserve of $21.6 million in the third quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement and logistics. Our three OEM customers are being supported directly, and we are working to restore normal order patterns as the recall notice is published.

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions (TDC).** Net sales grew 13.4% to $156.3 million, driven by hyperscale and colocation demand for both air- and liquid-cooled infrastructure. We won two new hyperscale awards in the quarter, and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger introduced in the second quarter is now in service with two hyperscale customers. TDC backlog grew 22.0% year over year to a record $574.2 million. This backlog converts to revenue over the next several quarters, with shipments building through the remainder of fiscal 2026 and into fiscal 2027, and it is the strongest indicator we have of fiscal 2027 revenue. We are prioritizing capacity and tooling for this business within our existing capital envelope.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to reflect the softer BCV environment, the recall-related order pause and the pace of Keystone realization. We now expect net sales of $1.66-1.70 billion, compared with our prior range of $1.78-1.84 billion, and adjusted EBITDA of $205-215 million, compared with our prior range of $255-270 million.

Project Keystone is our primary earnings lever. The program, which generated $6.2 million of restructuring charges this quarter, encompasses facility consolidation, sourcing and supply-chain redesign, and overhead reduction. Savings begin to build in the fourth quarter and reach the full $35 million run rate by the end of the second quarter of fiscal 2027. Together with completion of the recall program and the increasing weight of TDC in our mix, these actions underpin margin recovery into fiscal 2027.

As of September 30, 2026, we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q.

## Closing

This quarter demanded a great deal from our people — quality, plant, field service and customer-facing teams moved within days to stand behind a product issue and to protect our customers. That is the standard we hold ourselves to, and it is the same discipline we are applying to our cost structure and to the growth engine in data-center cooling. We are managing this company for the durable franchise it is becoming: a data-center cooling business growing at double digits on top of a core that we are fixing with speed and candour.

We thank our employees around the world, our customers and our suppliers for their partnership, and our shareholders for their patience and support.

Dana Whitcombe
